title: Analysis of serum Galectin-3 levels and correlation with bone metabolism parameters and bone density based on qCT or DXA measurements.
summary:
The clinical study presented here has been positively reviewed and approved by the responsible ethics committee. This clinical study is conducted exclusively in Munich at the Musculoskeletal University Center.
Your participation in this clinical study is voluntary. You will only be included in this study if you provide your written informed consent. If you choose not to participate, or if you later decide to withdraw from the study, you will not experience any disadvantages as a result.
The following text is intended to explain the purpose and procedures of this study. Afterwards, an investigator will discuss the study with you in detail. Please do not hesitate to ask about any points that are unclear to you. You will then be given sufficient time to consider your participation.
1. Why is this clinical study being conducted?
The main objective of this study is to investigate the development and pathophysiology of osteoporosis, with a particular focus on better understanding the role of Galectin-3 in human bone metabolism, as suggested by numerous prior publications.
2. What does participation in this clinical study involve?
If you decide to participate in this study, an additional blood sample of 4 ml will be taken alongside the routine blood sampling performed for osteoporosis diagnostics. This additional sample will be used exclusively to determine the Galectin-3 concentration as part of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria were: female, age ≥ 18 years, willing and able to give informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria were: secondary causes of osteoporosis (e.g., hyperparathyroidism, chronic steroid use), chronic inflammatory or malignant diseases affecting bone metabolism, renal insufficiency (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²), recent major surgery or fracture within 6 months, severe heart disease, rheumatic disease and malignancies.
